remaining_difference: Playback methods emit typed commands. Status, history, chapters, recent documents, version and track proxies read host context. The window proxy reads window observations and emits typed mutations. Media opens and external track loads use reviewed permissions. Exact window semantics and native command delivery across platforms remain open.

verification_status: Native libmpv and isolated Windows and Linux app tests
remaining_difference: Player entries expose getFlag, getNumber, getString, getNative, set, command and addHook. Typed writes cover playback options, reviewed transport options and reviewed external file lists. Commands cover playback, approved media loads and track additions, and application Quit. Hooks retain native priority order and release playback after errors or unload. Broader filesystem-granted properties and command forms, native rendering interactions and binary node values remain open.

Player event listeners support registration and removal. Selected IINA events and bounded mpv property subscriptions reach player entry workers. Full event coverage, ordering and native delivery remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and headless tests plus native Windows and Linux X11 console runs
remaining_difference: Player and global entries expose iina.console.log, warn and error. The log method formats multiple values and indents ordinary objects. The global console retains info. Developer Tool evaluates in the chosen live entry, collects logs and exception stacks, and inspects arrays, objects and global values in expandable rows. Up Arrow recalls commands from the transcript. Reload closes the old tool windows. Matched macOS presentation and interaction and engine-specific value formatting remain open.

Plugin-scoped @data and @tmp list/read/write/delete/move plus binary handle seek/read/write/close and showInFinder operations are bounded or permission-gated; @current paths use the current media directory and reviewed filesystem grant; @video/@audio/@sub aliases resolve current external track paths. Trash, Foundation encodings missing from or mapped differently by the WHATWG decoder, exact IINA path semantics, and native file-manager reveal verification remain open

verification_status: localhost HTTP and download transport tests
remaining_difference: The plugin API exposes GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, download and XML-RPC. Requests use reviewed permissions and manifest-domain checks. The transport tests cover redirect methods, credential handling and request limits. XML-RPC compatibility and third-party servers still need verification.

verification_status: QuickJS and local socket integration tests
remaining_difference: Player and global entries expose createServer, startServer, the four listener callbacks and sendText. Incoming messages expose text and Uint8Array data. Outgoing UTF-8 uses binary WebSocket frames. Riina requires a reviewed network-listener grant. Apple Network.framework waiting states and macOS desktop verification remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and headless regressions plus isolated Windows and Linux X11 playback
remaining_difference: Player entries expose prioritized key press and release and video-surface mouse press, release and drag. Plugins can normalize key names and read the active profile. Event replies share a bounded UI deadline. Key sequences, pressure-sensitive input and input captured by native menus remain outside the player route. Native macOS testing remains open.

verification_status: headless shortcuts and isolated Windows and X11 menu tests
remaining_difference: Global and player entries contribute ordered groups to the Plugin menu. Nested menus retain separators and disabled branches. More holds entries after the fifth top-level item per package. Selected leaves show a checkmark, and actions return to their owning entry. Shortcut conflict reporting, native Wayland interaction and matched macOS presentation and interaction remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and native libmpv tests plus Windows popup checks and Linux popup checks on X11 and Wayland
remaining_difference: Player realms expose list, count, add, remove, move, play, playNext, playPrevious and registerMenuItemBuilder. Playlist additions reuse reviewed media permissions and indexed edits resolve observed entry IDs. Sidebar and Music Mode menus use native Windows, X11 and AppKit presenters and a Wayland player-surface presenter. X11 and Wayland verified nested selection and shutdown with a menu open. Interactive Windows menu selection and native macOS desktop verification remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and storage tests plus isolated Windows and Linux settings WebViews
remaining_difference: Player and global entries share get, set and sync with manifest defaults. A package can declare a local preferencesPage with text, checkbox, radio and numeric field bindings. Closing the settings page or leaving Plugins saves pending edits to the package store. Native macOS interaction, matched sheet presentation, and import of IINA property lists remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and isolated Windows and Linux X11 application tests
remaining_difference: Player entries expose registerProvider, item and CUSTOM_IMPLEMENTATION. Declared providers appear in the subtitle menus and Settings, retain opaque results in their owning realm, and can search automatically. Downloads resolve through the plugin file scope and are attached only to the matching media generation. Matched macOS chooser appearance and third-party providers remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and isolated Windows and Linux utility workflows plus Windows credential persistence
remaining_difference: Utility entries expose helper lookup, scoped path resolution, bounded exec with streamed output, credential access, preferred languages, external opening, asynchronous file or folder selection, and synchronous confirmations and prompts. Native execution and external opening use distinct reviewed grants. Native credential-store round trips on Linux and macOS, interactive native file selection, and native macOS dialog conformance remain open.

verification_status: global and player menu ownership tested
remaining_difference: Separate global and player entry realms expose the broadcast message API. Plugin-created player instances, labels, targeted messages and full message delivery verification remain open.

verification_status: overlay runtime tests and isolated Windows navigation
remaining_difference: The overlay API emits validated effects and has a Windows native-video WebView presenter. Tests cover document, style, content and message effects. An isolated Windows run verified messages from consecutive package documents. Visible layering, pointer routing and other platform presenters remain open.

verification_status: X11 sidebar lifecycle and isolated Windows navigation
remaining_difference: Manifest sidebar tabs load confined package documents. Windows, macOS and Linux X11 use native WebView adapters. The isolated X11 checks covered opening, resizing, enable/disable, bidirectional messages and Quit from a focused sidebar. An isolated Windows run verified messages from consecutive package documents. Wayland embedding, native macOS behavior and matched geometry remain open.

verification_status: QuickJS and isolated Windows and Linux X11 and Wayland lifecycle tests
remaining_difference: Player and global entries can open a native WebView, load confined package files or Simple Mode content, exchange messages, and set window properties. Closing hides the page until reopening. Native macOS verification, matched geometry and titlebar appearance, and application-wide global-entry ownership remain open. Wayland placement follows the compositor.
Manifest parsing, package installation, permission review and transactional replacement are implemented. Live package management and broader third-party installer compatibility remain open.

Persistent entry workers load confined package modules and handle enable, reload, callback delivery and shutdown. Tests cover module loading, execution cancellation and reload. Full lifecycle ordering and third-party plugin behavior remain open.
